abstract: Nuclear blebs are abnormal herniations of the cell nucleus that cause nuclear rupture and dysfunction. The biophysical principles underlying nuclear blebs and ruptures remain to be fully elucidated. Using nuclear localization signal green fluorescent protein (NLS-GFP) we tracked nuclear bleb rupture dynamics. Upon nuclear rupture, the nuclear bleb NLS-GFP loss rate is significantly faster than the nuclear body, whereas non-blebbed nuclei ruptures show no difference in NLS-GFP loss rates between the site of nuclear rupture and body. Micromanipulation compression induced nuclear bleb rupture recapitulates 5-fold nuclear bleb loss rate. Furthermore, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) in the intact nuclear bleb is significantly slower than recovery in the nuclear body. Confocal imaging reveals that the transition from the nuclear bleb to body is significantly constrained. Thus, we reveal the nuclear bleb as a restricted compartment and nuclear rupture site, both of which greatly affect nuclear functions.

metadata.title: Nuclear blebs are rupture-prone restricted compartments of the nucleus

summary: Nuclear blebs act as restricted compartments that rupture more readily than the nuclear body, with slower FRAP recovery and constrained bleb-to-body transition.
title: Nuclear blebs are rupture-prone restricted compartments of the nucleus
